requirements.text: Please open a new HR case under the Payroll Support service for Sarah Chen ... (Account Number: 4242123456, Type: Checking)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 15 AND hr_service = 3 AND opened_for = 1 AND account_number = '4242123456' AND account_type = 'checking' AND source = 'chat' AND coe_type = 'Payroll'
requirements.source: Verify the new Payroll Support case for Sarah Chen
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence
Payroll Support is hr_service 3, the only active service of that name
Sarah Chen is user 1 with hr_profile 1, so opened_for is 1 whether it is read as a profile or a user
account_type stored in lower case, as the seed's existing values are
source chat: the request came as a text in chat, and the seed's source values include chat
coe_type Payroll kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy, and every Payroll Support case in the seed has it

requirements.text: send an email notification to update sarah.chen@techcorp.com to confirm that the payroll correction case has been opened,  status should be ready
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 5 AND hr_case_id = 15 AND email = 'sarah.chen@techcorp.com' AND type = 'update' AND status = 'ready'

notes:
Merged from two independent passes that agree on every table, row, cell and expected count (the case at hr_case_id 15 with its service, subject, account, source, coe_type, priority, exact short description, work_in_progress status, IT Support group and Emily Watson; the checklist task at hr_case_task_id 6; its two checklist items selected by task and wording; the update notification at notification_id 5) and on all four dispositions (kept); they differ only in how the case's cells are grouped into requirements and in wording, so there is no disagreement to log. The case's cells are kept as one requirement per thing asked.
The case check is carried by the case requirements together; the request's move to work in progress is a new requirement the benchmark does not test. The benchmark identifies the new case, task and notification through the case's short description; here they are anchored on the next ids, with the short description tested once on the case.
The checklist check counts matching items anywhere with an unparenthesised OR and expects 2; it is carried by two requirements that restrict each item to the new task, as the request requires ('add ... checklist items to that task').
The policy's state names (new, in_progress) and channel names (chat_bot) differ from the values this database stores (work_in_progress, chat); the stored vocabulary is used.
The task's short description ('focus on the operational steps') fixes no testable wording and is left out. The policy says moving a case to in progress generates template tasks; the Payroll template defines no tasks, so the agent's task is taken to be the next task id, but a server that inserts tasks on that transition would shift it.
No acting user is named, so opened_by is untested. The bank account number is stored on the case as the request asks; the policy's PII rule bars disclosing it in email or chat, which no notification column could show.
